content: Valacyclovir has been associated with the development of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura/hemolytic uremic syndrome (TTP/HUS), which can be fatal. This has been observed in patients with advanced HIV-1 disease, as well as in recipients of allogeneic bone marrow transplants and renal transplants who were administered doses of 8 grams per day during clinical trials of VALTREX. If clinical signs, symptoms, or laboratory abnormalities consistent with TTP/HUS are observed, treatment with VALTREX should be discontinued immediately. Acute renal failure has been reported in several patient populations: 1. Elderly patients, regardless of whether they have reduced renal function. When prescribing VALTREX to geriatric patients, caution is advised, and dosage adjustments are recommended for those with impaired renal function. 2. Patients with underlying renal disease who received doses of VALTREX exceeding the recommended levels for their renal function. Dosage reduction is necessary in patients with renal impairment to prevent complications. 3. Patients receiving other nephrotoxic drugs. In such cases, caution should be exercised when administering VALTREX due to the increased risk of renal toxicity. 4. Patients with inadequate hydration. Proper hydration must be maintained in all patients to reduce the risk of renal complications. If acute renal failure and anuria occur, hemodialysis may be required to restore renal function. Adverse effects on the central nervous system (CNS) have been reported in both adult and pediatric patients. These effects include agitation, hallucinations, confusion, delirium, seizures, and encephalopathy. Such reactions have been observed in patients with or without reduced renal function, as well as in those with underlying renal disease who received higher-than-recommended doses of VALTREX for their level of renal function. Elderly patients are particularly susceptible to CNS adverse reactions and should be monitored closely.
